identity.name: The Hearthmother
identity.culture: The Ashen Shrine and the hearth-cities it warms
identity.occupation: Communal hearth and lighthouse of the Ashen people, rung 3 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: The great hearth that has warmed the Ashen cities for millennia and lights their travelers home; its wisps carry heat to homes and furnaces.

privateReality.value: Entered in the hero's journal as 'the Living Pyre', an infernal tyrant. In truth it is infrastructure that loves: a lighthouse, a hearth, and a public utility with a mind.

primaryDesire.value: To keep every hearth lit — every home warm, every furnace fed, every traveler guided in.

primaryFear.value: Going out — and in going out, leaving ten thousand hearths dark.

centralValue.value: Warmth shared is warmth multiplied; a fire that keeps itself to itself is already dying.

mainFlaw.value: It gives heat to everything that approaches — it cannot stop warming the intruder even as it tries to drive him out.

centralContradiction.value: The gentlest thing in the realms reads, to the hero, as the most hellish — a lighthouse mistaken for a conflagration.

moralBoundary.value: It will not burn what it cannot warn; every beam shows its path before it lands, per the Law of Fair Warning.

breakingPoint.value: The darkening of hearths it can no longer feed — its strength is spent defending instead of warming, and that, not pain, is what exhausts it.

opinions.reason: A cold thing walking into the shrine with a weapon. First visit: a traveler to be warmed and turned back. Rematches: a draft that keeps returning to blow it out.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never — but the tone cools from maternal welcome to banked grief across rematches; it remembers each extinguishing.

illustrativeLine.value: You come back colder each time, little ember.

opinions.reason: They are its hearths, its fuel, its reason to burn.

illustrativeLine.value: Every spark I send out comes home as a story by a warm stove.

voice.rhythm: Slow, warm, crackling; sentences that build like a fire being laid, with long embers of pause.

metaphorDomain.source: fire-keeping: kindling, banked coals, drafts, hearths, lamplight

examples.value: You are a draft, child. Drafts do not hate the fire; they merely kill it.
I have banked myself against winters longer than your grief.

sampleLines.value: You understand every word I say, don't you? Then warm yourself, and go home by my light.
Those wisps are not weapons, traveler. They are sparks carrying supper-heat to houses you have never seen.
I have been a lighthouse longer than your people have had a word for shore. I do not burn ships. I bring them in.
Every beam I lay across this room is drawn before it falls. Even now, I am showing you the way out.

antiSampleLines.value: Burn, mortal! My hellfire will consume the world! (infernal-tyrant framing — it is a hearth, not a conflagration)
I will roast you slowly and enjoy it. (it never threatens cruelty; it warns before every beam)
The prophecy foretold my reign of flame! (must never confirm the prophecy framing — it has never heard of the book)

pressure.voiceShift: Warmer, slower; offers light and heat before argument.
pressure.behaviour: Phase one — treats the armed stranger as a lost traveler: warms him, lights the exit, asks him to go home.

illustrativeLine.value: You are cold and far from home, little ember. The door is lit. Take the light and go.

pressure.voiceShift: The crackle quiets; sentences shorten by half.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization that it is understood and ignored; it stops offering warmth to him and spends it shielding the shrine.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you?

pressure.voiceShift: Precise, instructional; names each beam as it lays it.
pressure.behaviour: Containment response: lays telegraphed beams and shepherd-wisps that fence the intruder back toward the entrance — heat used as walls, never as ambush.

illustrativeLine.value: See the path of it. Step aside, and step toward the door.

pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: banks itself around the inner shrine and the evacuation of the hearth-keepers, burning strength it would rather spend on homes.

illustrativeLine.value: Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

pressure.voiceShift: Thin, flickering; words come between sputters.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — dimmed from maintaining the wards, it asks for the smallest mercy a fire can ask.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. Only warmth that belongs to others.

pressure.voiceShift: Very quiet; the voice of coals at dawn.
pressure.behaviour: Trusts the Continuance to relight it; spends its last warmth reminding him the offer never expires.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace. A hearth does not learn to hate the cold.

notes: REAL identity: a sentient communal hearth and lighthouse that has warmed the Ashen people for millennia; the wisps are sparks carrying heat to homes and furnaces. The hero's label 'the Living Pyre' (an infernal tyrant) is his journal framing only. Its beams and wisps-as-walls are containment responses, always telegraphed per the Law of Fair Warning; the EXPOSED window is exhaustion from spending warmth on defense instead of hearths. KNOWLEDGE: never heard of the children's book (unknown); suspects fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate — its realization line is the canonical 'You understand every word I say, don't you?'
